meta.title: Surya Graha Mantra (Sun) | Japam
meta.description: Surya sun mantra 108 japa — Japam digital practice.

runs.text: Surya (the Sun) represents vitality and clarity in Navagraha worship.
Sunday japa with Om sooryaya Namaha is a common discipline.
Chant with a calm mind, offering salutation rather than demanding specific outcomes.

items: Community yagnas may align with season
Set daily 108 sankalpa for festival period
Keep fast/vrat rules from your family tradition

runs.text: Sunday sunrise is ideal; offer water (arghya) if doing puja.
The number 108 is one full round on a japa mala. Steady repetition calms the mind and deepens attention on the mantra’s meaning.
Some traditions prescribe 11 or 21 malas — ask your guru or priest for counts suited to your vow.

items: Chanting too fast and losing focus on the sound
Mixing multiple deity vows without guidance
Expecting only material results instead of bhakti and ethical living

runs.text: Home japa supports temple worship; it does not replace darshan. Visiting the temple on festival days or Saturdays strengthens family tradition.
Practise Surya japa in Japam with on-screen counting.

faqs.question: Exact festival date this year?
faqs.answer: Check Hindu panchang for your region — we avoid locking a Gregorian year in this guide.

faqs.question: How many japas per day?
faqs.answer: 108 minimum for many vows; some do 1008 on main day under guidance.

faqs.question: Guest mode OK?
faqs.answer: Yes for try; sign in to save progress across festival weeks.

faqs.question: Replace temple?
faqs.answer: No — digital japa supports home practice.

faqs.question: Join collective yagna?
faqs.answer: See Maha Japa Yagnas in Japam menu during campaigns.

disclaimer.text: This article is for educational and devotional practice only. Japam does not provide medical, legal, or financial advice. Results depend on personal faith and consistent practice. Mantra text and audio in the app are for japa support; consult your family priest or tradition for formal puja rules.
